_doc: WHY THE AVIANS WORK, measured after they were reported as the first models
that look right without a correction.
It is not joint quality. flyer_asonia is 1.3% faults and falcontip 1.9%,
against a roster median of 2.0% — ordinary. brutis, alphastar, vertigo and
the scorpion commander all sit at ZERO and none of them was reported as
It is the FOLD RATIO. The avians grow 3.72x and 1.63x from vehicle to
robot, against 4.4x for blackstar, 4.9x for dawnshade and 6.3x for grit.
A modest fold moves parts a short way, so a misplaced pivot displaces its
geometry proportionally less — the same error in the rig produces a
And falcontip, the LOWEST ratio in the roster at 1.63x, is the one that
reads best. A wing that folds is already most of the way to a wing that is
spread; a car that becomes a person is not.
THE LESSON IS NOT 'PREFER AVIANS'. It is that fold ratio predicts how much
rig error a chassis can hide, so it belongs in the screener as a
CONFIDENCE score rather than as a filter: a 6x fold needs its joints right
and a 1.6x fold forgives them. That is a better use of the joint fault
numbers than a flat threshold, and it says where to spend repair effort.
